root_idea.summary: The root centers on grief expressed outwardly through weeping, whether by shedding tears, uttering a lamenting cry, or experiencing grief without both of these manifestations.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence distinguishes audible lamentation from tears, while allowing either to predominate or occur alone. Derived forms extend the field to causing, competing in, feigning, or soliciting weeping.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the distinct Form IV causative verb.
Displayed under the singular active-participial citation form supported by the evidence; the Quranic occurrence is its plural form.

senses.definition: To weep or grieve, through shedding tears, uttering a lamenting cry, or either occurring alone.
senses.usage_conditions: Audible lamentation and tears may occur together or separately, and grief need not entail both. The verb can describe weeping as an expression of grief without requiring a particular bodily manifestation.

senses.definition: To weep for or over someone or something; to mourn or lament.
senses.usage_conditions: The person or thing mourned may be introduced with لِ or عَلَى. In the Quranic expression concerning the sky and earth weeping over them, the statement is understood either literally or figuratively; the construction is not restricted to a human subject.

senses.definition: To make or cause someone to weep.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction in which the person caused to weep may be stated or understood.
The supplied Quran occurrence is the plural form بُكِيًّا, used substantivally and rendered contextually as “weeping” or “weepers.”

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or figurative use predicated of a cloud.
Reported especially of a pigeon and similar creatures, and also attested of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with another in weeping and surpass him in it; to be the greater weeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III comparative or competitive construction concerning relative ability or intensity in weeping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prompt or provoke mourning for someone dead or for something lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized causative construction with عَلَيْهِ; this classical mourning context is distinct from the general Quran-attested causative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or feign weeping, or to strive or force oneself to weep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI reflexive or affected-weeping construction; the outward display need not reflect spontaneous grief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, request, or require weeping from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X construction expressing a desire or requirement that another person weep.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who weeps much; a habitual or frequent weeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive adjective or noun for a person characterized by abundant weeping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More given to weeping than another; a greater weeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective, distinct from the homographic Form IV causative verb.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The primary weeping, grief, tears, lamentation, and prepositional constructions are covered by the two Form I senses.
Cloud-related use is represented as a classical branch.
The singing use is represented separately.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form III entry.
Competitive weeping use is represented under the Form III headword.
The general causative and specialized mourning construction are both represented.
Affected or effortful weeping is represented under Form VI.
Feigned or displayed weeping is covered by the same Form VI meaning.
Pointer-only reference to the Form IV entry.
Seeking or requiring another's weeping is represented under Form X.
The intensive sense 'one who weeps much' is represented.
The speechlessness sense is explicitly questioned as possibly belonging to بكأ rather than بكي.

The active participle and its plural are represented by the normalized nominal form.
The comparative adjective is represented separately from the Form IV verb.

cautions: The Quranic nominal occurrence is the plural بُكِيًّا; it is presented under the supported singular active-participial citation form بَاكٍ.
أَبْكَى is represented both as the Quranic Form IV causative verb and, separately, as a classical comparative adjective meaning “more given to weeping.”
A Lane discussion of Form VI تَبَاكَى is retained as a classical derived-form meaning because no corresponding Form VI QAC form group is supplied.
No Maqayis entry was supplied; the root orientation is therefore based on the available direct lexical discussions.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:bky:36979:g2:main reports بَكِيٌّ for “a man unable to speak,” but the same unit suggests that the form may instead be بَكِئٌ from the separate root بكأ; the meaning is not assigned confidently to بكي.
